newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World Infra takes control of ATL.
newsitem.headline: New World Infra takes control of ATL.

text.p: New World Infrastructure Ltd will increase its holding in Sea-Land Orient Terminals Ltd (SLOT) and thereby its stake in Asia Terminals Ltd through the issue of new shares and a cash payment, the company said in announcement issued late on Monday.

The company said it was increasing its stake in Ready City Limited, whose principal asset is 33.34 per cent of the issued share capital of SLOT, for a total consideration of HK$1.59 billion. New World Infrastructure already holds a 41.5 percent stake in SLOT.

On completion of the agreement, the company will hold 91 percent of Ready City which, through SLOT, will raise its effective interest in Asia Terminals (ATL) to 54.17 percent. ATL is the operator of container terminal 3 in Hong Kong's Kwai Chung port.
The deal is to be completed on or before February 6, 1997.
New World Infrastructure will pay for the acquisition with the issue of 42.8 million new shares and the payment of HK$795.1 million in cash.
The value of the new shares is calculated on the basis of HK$18.5725 per share.
This represents a discount of about five percent from the closing price of HK$19.55 per share on November 6 and a discount of 16.34 percent to the closing price of the HK$22.20 on November 25.

The new shares represent 5.7 percent of the existing issued capital of New World Infrastructure and 5.3 percent of its enlarged issued capital. The total consideration of HK$1.59 billion represents 24.9 percent of the company's consolidated net assets as at June 30, 1996.
SLOT is principally engaged in the operations of container terminal 3 at Kwai Chung.
Asia Terminals is principally engaged in the operation of a container freight station and cargo distribution centre in terminal 3.
